skills_considered.reason: The discovery ledger is a research surface another batch owns; this wave's question is patient provenance and counting, so findings are proposed through commit candidates instead of ledger edits.
No source in this group tests a therapy against a mechanism; forging hypotheses from single-patient drug histories would manufacture a lead.
No compound is proposed as a candidate; anti-seizure medication histories in case reports are clinical descriptions, not molecules for BLOCK-1 triage.
Scientists do not touch the four current files; changes are proposed as commit candidates for a later BATCH_COMMIT.
No proposed change narrows or reverses a consolidated baseline claim; the triples are published in the candidates for an auditor to run.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed counts 2026-10-03: Scheffer IE[au] 676 records, 3 intersecting WWOX (this paper, the 2023 WWOX-DEE cohort and one other). A large international epilepsy-genetics consortium; the WWOX patient is one of 135 and is re-reported with RNA work in the same group's 2023 cohort.

field_density.note: Four PubMed records pair WWOX with migrating focal seizures; this is the first and its patient is re-described in the 2023 cohort.

multihop.note: All 49 references enumerated; the only WWOX-direct reference is Piard 2018/2019, resolved against its held Supplemental Table 1 (its E17K carrier, patient 12, has a different trans allele). The forward citation 36779245 (Oliver 2023) was resolved because it states that its patient 6 was briefly reported in this paper.

corpus_crossquery.note: Only FT-140 (full-text queue) names the paper; it calls the E17K occurrence overlap-confounded. The prior receipt FTR-20260921-31618474-01 is a verification of an extractor-damaged artefact with no gene symbols.

entries.proposition: The WWOX patient is compound heterozygous for a recurrent missense change and an intronic deletion whose splicing effect is predicted, not assayed, in this paper.
entries.snippet: We identified compound heterozygous variants in WWOX in Patient 93, a recurrent missense change (p.E17K)29 and a novel intronic deletion predicted to alter splicing.

entries.proposition: The paper's own Table 2 classifies both WWOX alleles as variants of unknown significance; the paternal allele is two intronic deletions detected by microarray.
entries.snippet: Paternal Intronic Deletions: Chr16:78,180,536-78,185,186 x1 and Chr16:78,200,089-78,218,016 x1 NA NA 0 NA NA NA CMA VUS

entries.proposition: The maternal E17K allele is classified VUS in Table 2.
entries.snippet: 93 WWOX Maternal Chr16:78133724G>A p.E17K rs780345312 02/196758 PD D 29 WES VUS

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table 1 places the two paternal deletions in introns 3 and 4, records a non-consanguineous female recruited in Australia, and says the patient was not previously reported.
entries.snippet: Compound heterozygous: c.49G>A p.E17K and 2x intronic deletions: intron 3 and 4, 16q23.1(78,180,536-78,185,186)x1 and 16q23.1(78,200,089-78,218,016)x1

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table 1 records Patient 93 as not previously reported.

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table 2 links the E17K allele to Piard patient 12, i.e. treats it as a different patient.
The cohort's 6.8 Mb deletion is a chromosome 2 deletion encompassing SCN1A and SCN2A, not a 16q deletion.
entries.snippet: Patient 54 had a heterozygous de novo 6.8 Mb deletion that included two known EIMFS genes, SCN1A and SCN2A.

entries.proposition: The WWOX patient developed epileptic spasms in addition to migrating focal seizures.
entries.snippet: Reported WWOX encephalopathy cases29 have had DEEs with infantile spasms and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome; our patient also developed epileptic spasms.
